title: Characterization of CD180 Protein Expression in Myeloid Hematological Malignancies by Flow Cytometry
official: Characterization of CD180 Protein Expression in Myeloid Hematological Malignancies by Flow Cytometry
summary:
CD180 is a cell-surface protein recently identified through proteomic analysis as a potential target of interest in myeloid hematological malignancies. It may have diagnostic and monitoring potential, particularly in acute myeloid leukemia (AML).

This monocentric, non-interventional, retrospective observational study aims to characterize CD180 expression by flow cytometry in pathological hematopoietic cells, particularly in AML, and in normal hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (CD34+ cells). The study will use residual blood and bone marrow samples collected during routine care and otherwise intended for disposal by incineration, together with relevant clinical and laboratory data.
conditions: Normal Hematopoietic Stem and Progenitor Cells
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adult patients aged 18 years or older.
* Pediatric patients aged 1 to 17 years.
* Patients with confirmed or suspected acute myeloid leukemia who have undergone bone marrow aspiration as part of the diagnostic or relapse assessment.
* Patients whose stem cells are being assessed using a blood or bone marrow sample.
* Patients and/or their legal representatives, where applicable, informed by letter of the use of residual sample material for research purposes.
* No written objection documented in the medical record to the reuse of personal data for scientific research.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients and/or their legal representatives, where applicable, who have objected to the reuse of personal data for scientific research.
* Samples more than 72 hours old.
* Clotted samples.
* Samples with insufficient volume (less than 10 microliters).
